color.safe: Your original color settings (materials) are never changed. A copy is made automatically and only the copy is changed.
color.where: Which part do you want to recolor?
color.noneInPart: No color settings were found for this part. Choose another part, or reassign items from another part's list using the menu on the right.
color.movePart: If the part is wrong, choose the right one here
color.nonLilToon: For non-lilToon materials, only the overall tint is changed.
toggle.intro: Checked items can be shown or hidden from the VRChat expression menu. Your avatar's original menu and animations are not changed.
toggle.none: No items for outfit toggles (outfits or accessories) were found.
toggle.pick: Items to add to the menu (these names appear in the menu)
toggle.bits: Sync usage: avatar {0} bit + this menu {1} bit (limit {2} bit)
toggle.bitsOver: Sync usage may exceed the limit. Please add fewer items (items added by other tools are not counted here).
toggle.removeConfirm: Remove the outfit toggle menu made by Kaihen Navi and restore how items were shown before it was created?
toggle.nothingPicked: Please check the items to add to the menu.
toggle.done: Created {0} outfit toggles. After uploading, find them under "Outfit toggles" in the VRChat expression menu.
toggle.howToUse: The menu uses Modular Avatar and is merged automatically when you upload. Items that look hidden in the scene will still be shown by default after uploading.
toggle.needMa: Creating the menu requires the free tool "Modular Avatar". Add it with VCC (or ALCOM) and open this screen again.
toggle.quickNote: The avatar is uploaded as set here (you can't switch it inside VRChat).
transform.which: Which item do you want to adjust?
transform.selectionInvalid: Click an item inside this avatar (such as an accessory) in the scene first.
transform.pickFirst: Choose the item you want to adjust above.
transform.none: No movable accessories were found. Click one in the scene, then press "Use the scene selection".
transform.skinnedWarn: This outfit deforms with the body, so moving it may not change how it looks.
transform.directionNote: Directions are from the avatar's point of view (right = the avatar's right hand side).
undo.toggle: Kaihen Navi: Create outfit toggle menu
undo.toggleRemove: Kaihen Navi: Remove outfit toggle menu
mine.autosave: Edits are saved to this avatar automatically. The original avatar is not changed.
mine.savedAt: Saved automatically at {0}. The original avatar is not changed.
mine.suggest: This avatar is not an edited avatar yet. Edits made now only live in the scene and are lost if you forget to save it. Turn it into an edited avatar so edits are saved automatically (the original stays as is).
mine.notYet: Not an edited avatar yet (edits only live in the scene)
mine.unlinked: This avatar is no longer linked to its prefab (e.g. it was unpacked). Save its current state as an edited avatar so it is easy to find later and edits are saved automatically.
mine.created:
Created the edited avatar "{0}".

From now on, edits are saved here automatically. The original avatar is not changed.
mine.failed: Could not create the edited avatar. Check the Console for errors.
avatars.renameTip: Changing the name also renames the file and folder
avatars.renameFailed: Could not rename. An avatar with the same name may already exist.
start.new.title: Create a new edited avatar
start.new.desc: Make an avatar for editing from one you bought. The original stays untouched.
start.existing.title: Edit an existing edited avatar
start.existing.desc: Pick an edited avatar you made before and continue.
start.looseHint: These avatars were placed in the scene directly and are not edited avatars yet.
new.pickBase: Choose the avatar to start from
new.noBase: No avatar prefabs were found. First, import the unitypackage of an avatar you bought on BOOTH or a similar store.
new.name: Name of the edited avatar
new.done:
Created the edited avatar "{0}".

Only this avatar is shown in the scene. Your edits are saved to it automatically. The original avatar is not changed.
existing.pick: Choose an edited avatar to edit
existing.none: You have no edited avatars yet. Start with "Create a new edited avatar".
existing.fullOnly: Making another version (e.g. a different outfit) and renaming are available in the full version.
current.label: Avatar you are editing
feature.outfit.title: Put on an outfit
feature.outfit.desc: Pick an outfit to make it follow the body's movements
outfit.intro: Choose an outfit made for this avatar to make it follow the body's movements. This uses Modular Avatar, so the original outfit and avatar files are not changed.
outfit.suggest: Outfits that seem to be for this avatar (click to put on)
outfit.afterTips: If an outfit overlaps one already worn, use "Set up outfit and accessory toggles" to hide it or switch it from the menu. If skin pokes through, use "Hide skin poking through outfits".
outfit.needMa: Modular Avatar is required to put on outfits. Add it to the project with VCC (or ALCOM).
outfit.setupFailed: Could not fit the outfit to the body. Check that it is made for this avatar. The outfit was placed inside the avatar; use "Restore" to undo.
pick.looksOutfit: "{0}" looks like an outfit (it contains body bones). Use "Put on an outfit" to fit it to the body. Use it here anyway?
pick.looksAccessory: "{0}" looks like an accessory (it has no body bones). Use "Add an accessory" to choose where to attach it. Use it here anyway?
attach.suggest: Accessories that seem to be for this avatar (click to choose)
attach.noBone: That place could not be found on this avatar. Choose another place.
attach.head: Head / face / ears
transform.whichHint: Adjust the position, rotation and size of attached accessories.
feature.body.title: Change body shape / height
feature.body.desc: Drag points on the silhouette to change length and width
body.intro: Drag a point on the silhouette on the left: up/down changes length, left/right changes width. Click a point first to choose a body part. The original avatar is not changed (this uses Modular Avatar).
body.needMa: Modular Avatar is required to change body shape. Add it with VCC (or ALCOM).
body.notHumanoid: This avatar is not set up as Humanoid, so its body shape cannot be changed.
body.head: Head
body.heightReadout: Current height: about {0} cm (the viewpoint adjusts automatically)
body.resetAllConfirm: Restore the original body shape and height?
body.dragHint: Drag a point up/down for length, left/right for width. Left and right parts change together.
body.dragHintWhole: You can also drag the waist point up/down to change height.
body.noArmature: The avatar's bone root (Armature) was not found, so height cannot be changed.
view.intro: This is where your eyes are in VRChat. If it is off, the floor looks too close or your body looks odd. The blue ball in the scene shows the current point.
view.readout: Current viewpoint: height {0} m, front/back {1} m
view.noEyes: Eye/head bones were not found, so it cannot be matched automatically. Use the arrows.
view.tip: Aim to place the blue ball between the eyes (just below the eyebrows), slightly in front of the face.
undo.viewAuto: Kaihen Navi: Align viewpoint with eyes
thumb.intro: Take a thumbnail for uploading. The VRChat SDK camera has a wide field of view that can distort faces, so this camera uses a narrower field of view.
thumb.howToUse: The image is saved as Thumbnail.png in the avatar's folder. Select it when uploading to use it as your thumbnail.
pink.intro: Finds pink materials and shows how to fix them. The most common cause is that the shader the avatar uses is not in the project.
pink.how.lilToon: Open the project in VCC (or ALCOM) and add "lilToon". It fixes itself once added.
pink.how.Poiyomi: Install Poiyomi Toon Shader (add its VCC repository or import the unitypackage). You may need to Unlock the materials afterwards.
pink.how.UnityChanToonShader: Add Unity-Chan Toon Shader (UTS2) to the project.
pink.how.Sunao: Add Sunao Shader to the project (distributed on BOOTH, etc.).
pink.missing: The shader in use was not found
pink.how.missing: Could not tell which shader it is. Check the avatar's README for required items and install that shader.
pink.how.locked: After installing the shader, select the material, Unlock it, then Lock it again.
pink.unsupported: This shader is not supported on this PC
pink.how.unsupported: Make sure the build target is PC (Windows). Some shaders do not work on Android (Quest).
pink.how.error: The shader version may be too old or too new. Reinstall the version listed in the avatar's README.
pink.missingMaterialHow: Put the original material into the empty slot under Materials in the Inspector. If unsure, check the same spot on the original avatar.
upload.new: Upload target: not uploaded yet (will be a new avatar)
upload.update: Upload target: {0} (updates the avatar you uploaded before)
upload.makeNewConfirm:
Upload next time as a new avatar?

The avatar you uploaded before stays as it is (not overwritten).
upload.conflict: This shares an upload target with another edited avatar ({0}). Uploading now would overwrite it. Set one of them to "Upload as a new avatar".
skin.intro: Skin can poke through outfits. The easiest fix is to use the shrink shape keys included in the body mesh. The original avatar is not changed.
skin.noBody: The body mesh was not found.
skin.noShrink: No shrink shape keys (e.g. Shrink) were found. Try "Show other shape keys" below, or use "Cut with Mesh Cutter (advanced)".
skin.noShapesAtAll: This body mesh has no shape keys. Use "Cut with Mesh Cutter (advanced)".
skin.tip: For "Always hide", move the value until the skin disappears. When an outfit is chosen, checked parts shrink only while wearing it (and come back when taken off).
skin.noCutter: The installed Modular Avatar has no Mesh Cutter. Update Modular Avatar with VCC (or ALCOM).
skin.cutterIntro: Mesh Cutter removes part of the body mesh only at upload time (the original is not changed). Choose an outfit to cut only while wearing it.
skin.cutterHow: Choose the area to cut in the Inspector (the skin mesh to cut is already set).
skin.cutterAdded:
Added and selected a Mesh Cutter. Choose the area to cut in the Inspector; the skin mesh is already set.

Use "Restore" to undo.
light.intro: Only brightness and shadow settings are shown. Original materials are never changed; a copy is made automatically before editing.
light.noLilToon: No lilToon materials were found. This feature is for avatars that use lilToon.
light.which: What do you want to adjust?
light.othersSkipped: {0} non-lilToon material(s) will not be changed.
light.preset.visible: Easier to see in dark places
light.minLightHint: The avatar never gets darker than this, even in dark worlds. Too high makes it look flat and glowing.
light.maxLightHint: The avatar never gets brighter than this, even in bright worlds. 100 helps avoid blown-out white.
light.unlitHint: Higher keeps the same brightness regardless of world lighting. Too high makes it look out of place.
light.shadowOff: {0} material(s) have shadows turned off. Shadow settings won't show shadows on them.
light.tip: Double-click a row to find it in the scene. Unchecked rows are not changed.
new.baseFirst: This is the first edited avatar made from this original, so a shared avatar base is also created. All edited avatars made from this original will share it. Change shared settings, such as walking animations, on this base.
new.baseReuse: This edited avatar will be created from this original's shared avatar base. Shared settings changed on the base (such as walking animations) also apply to this edited avatar.
existing.noBase: This edited avatar was created without a shared avatar base. Reconnect it to an avatar base to apply shared settings such as walking animations.
existing.rebaseConfirm:
Reconnect "{0}" to the shared avatar base of "{1}".

Your edits are kept. A copy of the current version is saved in this avatar's Backups folder just in case.
existing.rebaseDone: Reconnected "{0}" to the avatar base. Please check that it looks the same.
existing.rebaseFailed: Could not reconnect ({0}). The edited avatar was not changed.
skin.mesh: Which skin mesh? (numbers show the number of shrink shape keys)
feature.walk.title: Change animations
walk.intro: Swaps animations such as walking, sitting and emotes. The avatar's own settings are not changed; one small part that swaps the animations is added, so removing it always brings back the original.
walk.needMa: Changing the animation requires Modular Avatar. Add it to your project with VCC (or ALCOM).
walk.currentOriginal: Original (the one the avatar came with)
walk.conflict: Two animation replacements conflict. The avatar cannot be uploaded like this.
walk.scopeAll: All avatars made from the same original
walk.scopeAllHint: This changes the shared avatar base, so {0} edited avatar(s) made from it ({1}) will change. Avatars with their own animation keep theirs.
walk.noBase: This edited avatar was created without a shared avatar base. Select "Change avatar", open "Edit an existing edited avatar", and use "Reconnect to avatar base" to change animations for all of them at once.
walk.dropHint: Drag an animation controller (.controller) or a Modular Avatar prefab here
walk.tip: The animation is swapped when you upload. You can check it with Play mode or Gesture Manager.
walk.notWalk: "{0}" does not seem to contain settings to replace animations. Choose an animation controller (.controller).
walk.otherGimmick: Another animation setup ({0}) is already installed. Remove it with "Restore original animations" first.
walk.resetFirst: Another animation is already installed. Remove it with "Restore original animations" first.
walk.doneThis:
This avatar now uses "{0}".

Use "Restore original animations" to undo at any time.
walk.confirmAll:
Add the animation "{0}" to the shared avatar base. {1} edited avatar(s) made from it will change.

This cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z. Use "Restore original animations" to undo.
walk.confirmResetAll: Remove the animations from the shared avatar base and restore the original animations. This affects {1} edited avatars made from it.
walk.childConflicts: These edited avatars also have their own animations, causing a conflict. Open each one and click "Fix overlap (use this avatar's animations)": {0}
walk.fromBaseChanged: Shared animations overridden for this avatar
walk.which: Which animation do you want to change?
walk.layerWalkHint: Standing, walking, running, crouching and so on.
walk.layerSitHint: The pose when sitting on a chair.
walk.layerActionHint: Emotes (such as dances) and the AFK animation.
feature.menu.title: Tidy up the menu
feature.menu.desc: Hide or reorder an overly long menu
menu.intro: Choose which items appear in the avatar's built-in expression menu, reorder them, or rename them. The original menu files are not changed.
menu.needMa: Tidying the menu requires Modular Avatar. Add it to your project with VCC (or ALCOM).
menu.noMenu: This avatar does not seem to have a menu.
menu.extractHint: The current menu has {0} item(s). First, a copy of the menu is made inside this avatar for tidying up.
menu.hiddenNote: Unchecked items no longer appear in the menu. Only the button disappears; the function stays fixed in the state shown below.
menu.restoreConfirm:
Remove the tidied menu and go back to the avatar's original menu?

You can also use "Restore".
menu.tip: Use "Move to Other" to group items you rarely use and keep the menu tidy. Click a name field to rename it.
menu.useTip: Uncheck to hide this item from the menu
check.confirm:

check.fixed: Fixed the import settings of {0} model(s).
check.kind.normalsUnknown: Could not check the shape key normals setting (cannot be fixed automatically; please check the original file's settings)
mine.savedManually: Saved at {0}. The original avatar is not changed.
pick.scanExisting: Find items already in this project
pick.noOwnedResults: No items found. Try another name or scan for items.
pick.scanFailed: Could not scan for items. Please try again.
feature.innerColor.title: Change the color inside my hair
feature.innerColor.desc: Inner color: give only the inner layers a different color.
innerColor.intro: Choose your hair and press Preview to color the inside. Your original hair files stay unchanged.
innerColor.lilOnly: {0}: lilToon only (other material types are skipped).
innerColor.noSecond: {0}: parts without 2nd color support are skipped.
innerColor.noHair: No hair found. Hair is detected from names such as Hair.
innerColor.noHead: Could not find the head. The inside cannot be detected automatically for this avatar.
innerColor.thicknessHint: Colors areas hidden from outside. Higher values expand the colored area.
innerColor.heightHint: Higher values extend the color from the tips toward the center of the head.
innerColor.overwrite: {0} already uses 2nd color. Replace it with inner color? Restore will bring back the current settings.
innerColor.noUV: Could not read the texture layout for {0}.
innerColor.invalidUV: The hair texture layout could not be read.
innerColor.wideUV: Hair with very large texture repetition is not supported.
innerColor.importFailed: Could not import the color mask image.
innerColor.done: Color applied. After adjusting a setting, wait a moment for the preview to update.
innerColor.uvHint: Results depend on the hair. Hair sharing the same texture area also shares the color. Animated textures may move the colored area.
innerColor.measuring: Finding hidden areas of the hair. The first calculation may take a little time.
kono.noProducts: No products found. Try another name.
kono.invalidFolder: Choose the KonoAsset data folder containing the metadata folder.
kono.unsupportedVersion: [KaihenNavi] A KonoAsset file uses an unsupported data format and will be skipped. Supported format: version 3.
innerColor.checkingReferences: Checking which files are in use…
